layout.hierarchy: The large red title dominates. On the right, the green/red confusion matrices and branch diagram form the secondary visual focus. On the left, the formula and blue explanatory note support the definition.

visual_elements.description: Red-outlined definition/fraction box under the title. It contains two text lines separated by a horizontal rule: 'Correctly Classified (as Positive)' above and 'Total Classified as Positive (either Correct and Erroneous)' below.
Yellow-filled Meaning callout with red bold header 'Meaning' and black sentence '% of what you Predicted as POSITIVE is Actually Positive'.

Precision formula block: red bold label 'Precision =' beside a stacked fraction with numerator 'TP' and denominator 'TP + FP'. Small callouts read 'Positive Classified as +ive' under TP and 'Negative Classified as +ive' under FP. A green bracket under both callouts is labeled in red italic 'All Samples classified as Positive'. To the right, the worked example reads 'Precision= 10/(10+2) = 83.3%'.

Light blue note box with two lines: 'Higher Precision value DOES NOT mean you correctly retrieved more Positive samples.' and 'It means I HIGHLY trust you if you said this sample is Positive'. Emphasis is shown with bold/caps on DOES NOT, more, and HIGHLY.

Confusion-matrix template. Column header 'Predicted as' spans P and N; row header 'Actual' is vertical on the left. Cells: Actual/Predicted P = TP, Actual/Predicted N = FN, Actual N/Predicted P = FP, Actual N/Predicted N = TN. TP and TN are green-filled; FN and FP are light/white with red text.

Example confusion matrix with the same 'Predicted as' P/N columns and vertical 'Actual' row header. Cells: Actual P row = 10 and 20; Actual N row = 2 and 68. The 10 is highlighted in a blue circle, 68 is green-filled, and 20 and 2 are plain.

Two side-by-side branch diagrams. Left header 'Positive' in red; right header 'Negative' in green. Each has a small airplane icon. Positive branch: red circle 30 branches down to red circle 10 labeled TP and green circle 20 labeled FN. Negative branch: green circle 70 branches down to green circle 68 labeled TN and red circle 2 labeled FP. Red arrows show the branching/flow.
Small yellow circular badge at the top-right corner containing the black number 8.

imagery: Two small gray airplane icons, one beneath the red 'Positive' header and one beneath the green 'Negative' header, simple flat illustration style, in the right-lower diagram.
typography_notes: Sans-serif, Arial-like. Title is very large, bold, red. Section headers such as 'Meaning', 'Positive', and 'Negative' are bold; 'Positive' is red and 'Negative' is green. Body text is black. The precision formula uses a stacked fraction. Short matrix labels are all caps. 'All Samples classified as Positive' is red italic. The blue note uses black text with bold/caps emphasis.
animation_state: No animation or partial build is indicated; all elements appear fully revealed.
recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to light gray #F2F2F2. 2. Add the title 'Precision' top-center in large bold red #EE0000. 3. Under the title, place a red-outlined box from about 4% to 67% width. Put 'Correctly Classified (as Positive)' on the first line and 'Total Classified as Positive (either Correct and Erroneous)' on the second line, with a horizontal rule between them. 4. Add a yellow #FFFF00 Meaning box on the left with red bold 'Meaning' and the sentence '% of what you Predicted as POSITIVE is Actually Positive'; bold/color the words Predicted, POSITIVE, and Actually Positive as shown. 5. Add the formula area: red bold 'Precision =' with a stacked fraction TP over TP + FP. Under TP add 'Positive Classified as +ive'; under FP add 'Negative Classified as +ive'. Add a green bracket beneath both callouts labeled in red italic 'All Samples classified as Positive'. 6. To the right of the formula, add the black text 'Precision= 10/(10+2) = 83.3%'. 7. Add a light blue #DDEBF7 note box at bottom-left with the two exact sentences about higher precision not meaning more retrieved positive samples. 8. Build the top-right confusion matrix: header 'Predicted as' over P and N, vertical row header 'Actual', cells TP, FN, FP, TN; fill TP and TN green #00B050 and keep FN/FP light with red text. 9. Build the second matrix below it with the same headers and cells 10, 20, 2, 68; highlight 10 in blue #0070C0 and fill 68 green #00B050. 10. Add the right-lower diagram with red header 'Positive' and green header 'Negative', a small airplane icon under each, circles 30/10/20 and 70/68/2, red arrows, and labels TP, FN, TN, FP. 11. Add a small yellow circle with black '8' at the top-right corner.
